item.text: I’ll read the three note parts in order, build the question and position map, then run the required check and fix any reported issues.

item.aggregated_output:
<<11:22 notes, part 0 of 0..2>>
[MUQATIL:11:22/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | “La jarama” means certainly: these unbelievers are the greatest losers in the afterlife.
[TAB-FULL:v12p373#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | They are the greatest losers because they exchanged their homes in Paradise for the homes of the people of Paradise in Hell; al-Tabari also explains لا جرم as an idiom of certainty, literally associated with earning sin and used for inevitability.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019#2/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | لا جرم means 'indeed' or 'yes'.
[NAHHAS:v2p277/r1] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الخليل وسيبويه والفراء ومحمد بن يزيد | reports | These grammarians say لا جرم means “truly”; أن is nominative. Al-Khalil says لا marks the statement as a reply, not an opening utterance.
[NAHHAS:v2p277/r2] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq takes لا as denying the supposed benefit and جرم as their deed earning loss, so أن is accusative.
[NAHHAS:v2p277/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisaʾi explains لا as no denial or prevention of the outcome, and lists forms لا جرم, لا عن ذا جرم, لا أن ذا جرم, and a Fazara form without mīm.
[NAHHAS:v2p277/r4] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra adds dialects لا ذا جرم among Banu Amir and لا جرم with a damma on jīm among some Arabs.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One interpretation treats لا as an emphatic extra particle, so the phrase means that they truly are the greatest losers in the afterlife; the following line illustrates جرمت as causing or deserving an outcome.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The line about the thrust that made the Fazāra tribe angry uses جرمت in the sense of causing or making an outcome certain.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس؛ أكثر المفسرين | reports | Lā jarama means surely, certainly.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Lā jarama originally meant “no escape” or “inevitably,” later becoming an emphatic “truly” and sometimes functioning like an oath.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الزجاج؛ الأزهري؛ ابن الأنباري | prefers | Al-Zajjāj says lā denies the assumed benefit and jarama means earned: their deed earned loss; al-Azharī calls this one of the best explanations, and Ibn al-Anbārī analyzes jarama as a past verb with an implicit subject referring to disbelief.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · قوم | reports | Another explanation treats lā as extra, so their deed earned them regret.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الأخفش؛ سيبويه | reports | They take lā as a rejection of the disbelievers’ claim and jarama as “deserved/was certain”; the cited poem uses jaramat to mean that a spear thrust made Ghatafān angry.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء؛ أبو العباس | rejects | They reject that interpretation, reading Ghatafān as accusative: the wound caused the tribe to become angry.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | Lā jarama means truly; another says rather indeed, and al-Farra glosses it as without doubt. They are the greatest losers in the afterlife even though all are losers.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · سيبويه والخليل | reports | They take lā jarama as surely or truly; other grammarians say no doubt, no escape, or necessarily, also attributed to al-Khalil, while al-Zajjaj parses lā as rebuttal and jarama as earning, making their deeds earn them loss.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الزجاج والكسائي | reports | Al-Zajjaj places an in the accusative after lā as rebuttal, whereas Sibawayh takes it in the nominative; al-Kisaʾi says lā jarama means no turning away or prevention.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The sense of cutting may underlie jarama, while the earning sense is supported by poetry and by the gloss that a tribe’s jarīma is its earner; Jarir’s line can bear either sense.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Lā jarama has dialect variants including lā dhā jarama, lā an dhā jarama, lā ʿan dhā jarama, and lā jar with the mīm dropped through frequent use.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Lā jarama has variant forms in Arabic, including lā dhā jarama, lā an dhā jarama, lā ʿan dhā jarama, and a shortened lā jar due to frequent use.
[TABRISI:11:20-22/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj parses lā jarama as denying what they thought would benefit them, so their conduct earns the greatest loss; another explanation takes the expression as “necessarily” or “surely,” a decisive assertion that they are the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says lā jarama means “truly.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says lā jarama originally meant “there is no escape or doubt,” then frequent use made it equivalent to “truly”; its root is jarama, to earn sin.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj construes lā as denying benefit: their deeds do not benefit them; rather, they earned loss in the Hereafter.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbari says lā answers unbelievers who think punishment will be diverted, then jarama begins a new clause; jarama either means their unbelief earned punishment or that punishment was made sure, with a poem supporting the latter.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The various dialect forms—lā jarama, lā jarama without mīm, lā dhā jarama, and related forms—all mean “certainly.”
[RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | They are the greatest losers because the worldly thing they chose over the noble faith cannot endure and will perish.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ says lā jarama means inevitably or without doubt, and through frequent use came to mean truly.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · النحويون | reports | One grammatical analysis takes lā as negation and jarama as cutting: nothing can cut off the certainty that they will be the greatest losers.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj says lā denies the benefit they expect and jarama means earning: their conduct earns loss in this life and the next; al-Azharī calls this the best account. | mentions 5:2
[RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · سيبويه والأخفش | reports | Sībawayh and al-Akhfash take lā as a reply to unbelievers and jarama as “is true”: their unbelief makes punishment and loss rightfully occur; a poetic line uses the root for making a consequence certain.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil and Sibawayh take “la jarama” as “certainly,” treating it as one indivisible expression; “anna” is nominative. Al-Farraʾ and Muhammad ibn Yazid also transmit this analysis.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الخليل | reports | A second interpretation from al-Khalil and al-Farraʾ makes “la jarama” mean “inevitably” or “without doubt.”
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj parses “la” as denial of the claim that idols benefit, and “jarama” as “earned”: their deed earned loss, with the implied subject omitted and “anna” in the accusative; he supports the root with poetry.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisaʾi says “la jarama” means there is no restraint or prevention from their consequence.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Another explanation takes the expression as “no cutting can cut it off,” with the agent suppressed through frequent use; the root means cutting or stripping, as in harvesting dates, shearing wool, and taking meat from bones.
[QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النحاس | reports | Al-Nahhas reports four forms from al-Kisaʾi—“la jarama,” “wa-la ʿan dha jarama,” and “wa-la anna dha jarama” among them—and notes Fazarans' form without mīm; al-Farraʾ adds “la dha jarama” and a form with ḍamma on jīm.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Lā jarama means certainly; no one in the afterlife is more plainly or greatly a loser than they are.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They are the greatest losers in the afterlife because they led others astray and turned away themselves.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | One analysis takes لا as rejecting a preceding claim, جرم as acquired, and the whole as saying their claim earns them loss in the afterlife.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | A second analysis treats لا جرم as a compound meaning truly, with their loss as the subject of what is true.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | A third analysis understands the expression to mean inevitably.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الخليل وسيبويه | reports | Al-Khalil and Sibawayh analyze لا جرم as a fixed compound meaning “indeed,” with the following clause raised as its subject.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحوفي | reports | Al-Hawfi treats جرم as negated by لا, nominative as a topic, with أن and its clause as predicate; other grammarians take the construction to mean inevitably or no opposition/prevention.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj rejects compounding. Another analysis makes جرم a past verb meaning earned, with an implicit subject and the following clause as object; poems illustrate that root. Al-Nahhas and al-Farraʾ report dialect variants.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 7
